title: Kernel formula for finite constant quotient maps.
statement: theorem constant_quotient_kernel (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A) (n : ℕ) (U : C) : RingHom.ker ((quotient J A I n).hom.app (op U)).hom = Ideal.span (Set.range (fun a : ↥(I ^ (n + 1)) ↦ (constantSection (J := J) (a : A)).val (op U)))

proof.text: Choose a finite family g generating K = I^(n+1), using IsNoetherian.noetherian and Submodule.fg_iff_exists_fin_generating_family. Ideal.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun supplies coefficient functions c_i on K. Extend them to all of A by zero outside K.

Extend each set function c_i : A → A to the underlying constant sheaf. Conjugate sheafifyMap of the constant natural transformation by sheafifyComposeIso for forget CommRingCat. The sheafComposeIso_inv_fac, toSheafify_naturality and sheafComposeIso_hom_fac identities show that this extension sends the constant section a to the constant section c_i(a). This construction does not assert that c_i is a ring map.

For a section x killed by the quotient, form y = sum_i c_i(x) * constant(g_i). The image sieve of the constant-ring sheafification unit covers U (Presheaf.imageSieve_mem). On a member x is represented by a coefficient a. Naturality shows that the constant quotient class of a is zero. Local injectivity of the quotient sheafification unit gives a further covering equalizer sieve (Presheaf.equalizerSieve_mem) on which a lies in K. There the chosen coefficient identity and naturality give y = x. Apply sheaf separatedness twice to obtain y = x on U. The sum y lies in the ideal generated by the constant sections from K.

Conversely, naturality of the sheafification unit identifies the quotient of the constant section a with the constant section of the quotient class of a. For a in K this is zero. Ideal.span_le therefore puts the entire generated ideal in the kernel. Antisymmetry proves the stated equality, without changing its hypotheses.
